key_insight: This paper makes in-the-wild egocentric 3D hand-object pose estimation more practical by adding dense contact supervision and a new real-world dataset. The key idea is that accurate hand-object reasoning needs not just pose labels, but detailed contact correspondences from everyday scenes.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of estimating 3D hand-object pose from first-person RGB video in real-world settings, where occlusions, ambiguous hand-object contact, and limited supervision cause existing methods to generalize poorly.
method: Introduces EPIC-Contact, an in-the-wild egocentric dataset with 2.3K clips and 62.3K frames.
Provides dense, bijective 3D hand-object contact correspondences along with posed meshes for supervision.
Uses this data to better train models for robust hand-object pose estimation under severe occlusion and contact ambiguity.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper offers a stronger supervision signal and a realistic benchmark for improving first-person 3D interaction understanding. It can help systems become more reliable in AR/VR, robotics, and human-computer interaction applications.

paper_title: Towards in-the-wild Egocentric 3D Hand-Object Pose Estimation
paper_authors: Siddhant Bansal, Zhifan Zhu, Shashank Tripathi, Jiahe Zhao, Michael J. Black
